lexical.anchor: Can two independent engineers implement the same KnowledgeOS kernel without reading the historical research corpus?

rationale_evidence.anchor: C5 — IMPLEMENTATION READINESS … A state over the eight ratified primitives … Nothing that changes that state
rationale_evidence.statement: States what an engineer can build today without inventing semantics: a state over the eight ratified primitives carrying I-1..I-12 as constraints, enforcing policy stratification (I-11) and the authority boundary (A6/I-4/DC.Auth) with evidence composition obeying I-5/I-6 — but no legal operation or transformation is canonically defined, postconditions are undecidable without state equality, and commit executes as the identity function.

rationale_evidence.anchor: DECIDES NOTHING. It computes consequences of recorded statuses
rationale_evidence.statement: States the script's own epistemic scope: it builds the construct dependency graph from evidence already recorded elsewhere (handoff/05, TG-register, GN-77/84) and computes consequences (closure, blocked-construct classes, topological critical path, minimum implementable subset, one sensitivity variant) without making any new determination of what is or is not required.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Six blockers. Three require governance, three require derivation. None requires new theory discovery
rationale_evidence.statement: States the derived critical path to an implementation-ready KnowledgeOS specification: (1) which K is canonical [governance], (2) enumerate the invariant register ℐ [derivation], (3) state identity+equality [derivation], (4) run the operation-necessity test then ratify a registry [derivation then governance], (5) typed rejection semantics and the Reject/I-12/Article-8 contradiction [governance], (6) define delta's signature/pre/post/partiality/composition [derivation] — every one a decision about, or formalization of, material already present.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Blocker 1 which K — no artifact reconciles them · Blocker 2 ℐ — now recorded but not enumerated · Governance 1/25 · Operations 0/25 canonical · Transformations 0/25 · 99 cells 88 empty ... None [closed]. Consistent with 08: the blockers are decisions, and no decision was taken in this material. Steps 282–285 and the external research improved the description of the gap and did not reduce it.
rationale_evidence.statement: Register-update summary: no blocker is closed by the Steps 282-285 material and the external_research review; the work is explicitly characterized as improving the *description* of the gaps (blocker visibility, ℐ recorded in the dependency chain, ratification mechanism designed) without reducing the gaps themselves — two new gaps (G-68, G-69) are added and zero are closed.

# readiness-dependency-graph-minimum-implementable-kernel

**Scope(s):** OBJECT · **Row count:** 17 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** CONTESTED · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** 18 vs 15 required constructs, 3 unblocked (Provenance, RelationType, Assertion), InvariantReg -> O_core -> Operations -> Transformation -> {Rejection,Replay} · **Aliases:** gap-discovery readiness commission, minimum implementable KnowledgeOS

**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):**
Ungrouped — no mechanical signal connected this label to any other in P2a.

## Sources (how this label entered the ledger)

- **OBJECT-INDEX**, batch B0049, scope OBJECT: A computed (not preferred) construct-dependency graph and topological critical path for a minimal reference KnowledgeOS kernel (able to hold state, transition it legally, reject illegally, replay from history). The kernel's transitive requirement set is 15 (structural-invariants-only reading) or 18 (structural+epistemic reading) constructs out of the 25 the research programme produced -- the answer is undetermined by +/-3 because the mandated invariant register ('ℐ', G-67) has never been enumerated. Of the required set, only 3 (Provenance, RelationType, Assertion) are unblocked; the sole ratified construct (Policy) is conditional-OUT of the kernel; 0 of the 15-required-under-either-reading constructs carry a governance act. The severed segment InvariantReg -> O_core -> Operations -> Transformation -> {Rejection, Replay} is strictly linear with no parallel route. The existing EKP implementation (knowledge-lint, GovernanceLineageGraph, orphan_document) is exactly the unblocked structural sub-kernel, and nothing more can be added without passing the first blocker (which K is canonical).
